newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand ended a hectic late afternoon session more than two cents firmer below the key 4.59 level as foreign and local institutions offloaded dollars into the market, forex traders said.
The unit saw a brief flurry during the mid-morning session, moving stronger, but ranged tightly between 4.59 and 4.60 during the day before a rollercoaster ride in the late afternoon.
It ended the day at 4.5850/5900 on the dollar from 4.6085/6135 at Monday's close after an intraday low of 4.5850 bid.
"Offshore institutions, local institutions and mining houses sold dollars in the afternoon and it looks as if sentiment is changing," a senior forex trader said.
Another senior trader said there had been good local and offshore two-way trade on the day with the rand ticking all the way down to a 4.5850 low during the late afternoon session.
"A close below 4.60 brings into play a possible stab at 4.55 and if we can close the week below 4.60 then things are obviously looking up," the trader said.

Both the bond and the currency markets were awaiting the release of third quarter GDP figures and money supply and private credit extension data, due for release on Thursday and Friday, although forex traders said the figures would be more significant for the bond market.
The rand further extended gains against sterling, firming to 7.6509/6638 from 7.7228/7357 on Monday and was last trading at 0.3326/3332 marks from 0.3289/3294 marks previously.
Long bond yields ended the day stronger on the rand's gains and better U.S. bonds but failed to break through the important 15.82/83 percent level on the downside.
"The rand is looking good, U.S. bonds are stronger and I would say sentiment is firm," a bond trader at one of the "big four" banks said.
He said the 15.82/83 percent level was the decisive one to break on Wednesday.
"If 15.82 percent goes we could see a test of 15.65 percent...if not the market should range between 15.82 to 15.89 percent," he added.
Other traders said expectations for a third quarter GDP figure of around 2.5 percent from 3.5 percent would be bullish for the local bond market.
Money market and private credit extension data, on the other hand, were expected to be negative but traders said last week's one percentage point Bank rate hike had put a top on the market weakening.
The Reserve Bank last Thursday hiked the Bank rate to 17 percent from 16 percent.
At 1419 GMT the key R150 bond was at 15.84 percent from 15.89 percent previously.

On the money market, banks quoted their three-month NCD rates unchanged at between 16.95 percent and 17.00 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also steady at between 16.30 and 16.60 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the shortage higher at 9.383 billion rand on Monday from 8.956 billion rand on Saturday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners sold a net 128.74 million rand worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying a net 41.25 million rand worth of bonds on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 4.43 billion rand on Monday from 5.12 billion rand on Friday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
